correctness.rationale: For both run lengths >=2, all six subgroups of S3 give exactly two factor-orbit counts, with one missing integer. When a run length is one, every factor is either all-zero/one-hot or a one-hot phase repeated in full blocks with an optional partial block. A diagonal subgroup with prescribed orbit counts realizes all intermediate values. Exact-boundary proofs and subgroup embeddings were reconstructed. Running verify.py from its actual supplied path tested 1,662 positive instances plus all six subgroups at 49 negative parameter pairs. Finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural complete classification for every binary necklace with exactly two circular monochromatic runs, as opposed to isolated numerical cases. The theorem identifies a sharp combinatorial boundary between singleton and nonsingleton runs and constructs group witnesses for every factor length in the positive case, while the negative case has an exact three-letter obstruction. This gives uniform mathematical structure absent from the fixed-input finite criterion and contributes a nontrivial family to the recently posed classification problem.
